newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends 1996 narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends 1996 narrowly mixed.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures ended an abbreviated pre-New Year holiday trading session narrowly mixed with the chunk of the activity centred on nearby switch activity.

Dealings were slow with many players were away from their desks ahead of the holiday. The market is now closed, reopening on Thursday. "I thought we might have seen a bit more fireworks on the Jan/March spread as there are still some short funds in the market in Jan," said one.
"I thought they would cover by now but they haven't done. There's fairly hefty open interest in January."
The trade is long and is willing to sell but at a premium, the trader said.
The day's volume reached 1,430 lots, centred on Jan/March and Jan/May spread.

January was $10 firmer at $1,260 a tonne but benchmark March was $1 off at $1,236. The Jan/March spread saw active trade at $25-$26 after touching a high of $30-$32 while March/May was dealt at $26. Looking ahead, analysts said the coffee market could be heading for a choppy 1997, making it harder for players to trade.

"For the most part in 1997, the expected market movement picture is very uncertain because the various monthly cycles are in direct contrast to the generally expected seasonal biases in coffee," US brokerage Merrill Lynch said in a report. --Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
